en: Vulcan Point is a small island located inside the main crater lake of Taal Volcano, which sits on a larger island inside Taal Lake.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous worldwide for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape, which was formed by centuries of alternating layers of lava and ash.
During the dry season, the grass covering Bohol's Chocolate Hills dries up and turns chocolate brown, giving the unique geological formation its famous name.
The massive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo released so much ash and sulfur dioxide into the atmosphere that it temporarily cooled the entire Earth.
The Galathea Depth in the Philippine Trench is the third deepest point in the world's oceans, reaching nearly 10,540 meters below sea level.
The small island province of Camiguin uniquely has more volcanoes, totaling seven, than it has municipalities, which only number five.
The Philippines sits at the heart of the Coral Triangle, an area containing the highest diversity of coral and fish species on Earth.
The Philippines is a global biodiversity hotspot where more than half of its plant and animal species are found nowhere else on Earth.
The Tabon Caves in Palawan are known as the cradle of Philippine civilization because they contain the oldest human remains ever found in the country.
Hikers climbing Mount Pulag, the second highest peak in the Philippines, often experience a magical sea of clouds that forms above the grassy summit.
The Pasig River is technically a tidal estuary because its water flow direction reverses depending on the water levels between Manila Bay and Laguna de Bay.
The navigable portion of the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River stretches for 8.2 kilometers, making it one of the longest underground rivers in the world.
